strings.aboutBlurbTitle: Pulsar :: A GUI Wrapper for Nebula
strings.aboutBlurbDescription: Pulsar is a cross-platform, graphical user interface wrapper for Slack’s Nebula command line client, which was developed to make it easier for non-technical users to connect to a Nebula mesh network. Like a pulsar inside a nebula, it sends out a regular pulse to make the connection possible. While it is best used for connecting to a single Nebula mesh network, Pulsar has the capability to connect to up to five networks simultaneously, provided the networks have differing IP address ranges. It makes setting up the connections easy through the Settings page.
strings.aboutBlurbNebulaInfo: For security, Pulsar does not provide the Nebula command line executable file. The user needs to download and install it themselves and either add it to the system path or else point Nebula to the executable file. Because Nebula opens a special encrypted tunnel to the mesh network, the executable requires administrative privileges. The request dialog for these privileges will be triggered when the Connect button is clicked. It will trigger separately for each connection, so if you have multiple connections, you will see multiple privilege elevation dialogues.

strings.aboutLogsBlurb: The live logs for the current connection(s) can be observed in the boxes below. By default, these will update every 30 seconds. You can disable the live update by switching off the corresponding Refresh log automatically switches. You can also update the logs manually with the Refresh Log Now buttons. If you have multiple connections enabled, each connection is tracked separately.
strings.aboutLogsTooSmallTextWarning: The window size is too narrow to display the connection logs.
strings.settingsTooSmallTextWarning: The window size is too narrow to display the content.
strings.tooSmallTextMitigation: Please resize the window to access the content.
strings.switchCloseOnWindowLabel: Exit Pulsar when connection window is closed
strings.switchCloseOnWindowBlurb: If this is enabled, Pulsar will shut down when the user closes the main connection window. Disable this item to make sure that Pulsar keeps running in the status area even when the window is closed.
strings.switchMultipleConnectionsBlurb:
If you select this item, then Pulsar will allow you to connect to up to five separate Nebula instances simultaneously. 
                                    If left unchecked, Pulsar will connect to only one Nebula instance.
strings.inputPingIntervalBlurb: Defines how often Pulsar pings a random lighthouse to make sure that the Nebula network is up.
strings.settingGeneralSettingsNebulaBlurb: Select where Pulsar will look for the Nebula binaries.
strings.nebulaBinariesSysPathBlurb: Look for the Nebula binary in the system path.
strings.nebulaBinariesFilePathBlurb: Select the exact path to the Nebula executable below.
strings.txtNebulaBinaryNotFound: Could not find nebula executable file.
strings.txtNebulaBinaryNotFoundExplanation: Pulsar will not be able to connect to the Nebula network. Please either add the path to the directory with the executable file to your system path, or else directly point to the location of the nebula executable file.
strings.txtNebulaCertBinaryNotFound: Could not find nebula-cert executable  file.
strings.txtNebulaCertBinaryNotFoundExplanation: Pulsar will function without the nebula-cert executable. However, Pulsar will not be able to determine the validity of the connection authentication certificates or the IP address of your node. To rectify this, make sure the nebula-cert executable file is in the same directory as the nebula executable file.
strings.connectionListingBlurb: The following connections are available for connection to Nebula networks using Pulsar. Enable a connection by flipping the switch at the front. Any connection that has not been configured cannot be enabled.
strings.connectionEditHeadingBlurb: Pulsar uses this profile to connect to the designated nebula network as a node. You can edit the information for this profile using the fields below. Be sure to save the connection profile before continuing.
strings.settingsSwitchAutoConnectLabel: Automatically connect node to Nebula network on startup
strings.settingsSwitchKeepAliveBlurb: This option will ping a random lighthouse as frequently as defined under the Ping Interval option in General Settings.
strings.settingsSwitchNoPingBlurb: Prevent the connection from pinging the lighthouse at all. This can only be enabled if the connection is not kept alive. Only enable this if you have a slow connection or your lighthouse is being overwhelmed.
strings.connectionEditSectionAuthBlurb: The PKI certificates defined below make it possible for this node to authenticate with the Nebula infrastructure.
strings.connectionEditSectionFirewallBlurb: The data here generally should not need to be edited on a client.
strings.connectionEditSectionAdvancedConfigBlurb: For more configuration options, you can edit the Nebula node connection configuration file directly.
strings.connectionEditSectionAdvancedConfigWarni: Warning! If this is done incorrectly, the entire connection can stop working! Only edit the configuration file directly if you know what you are doing.
strings.connectionEditSectionResolveHosts: Resolve Host Names on Nebula Network
strings.connectionEditSectionResolveHostsBlurb: Below is a list of host names that resolve to IP addresses on the Nebula mesh network. These will be written to your system's hosts file when Pulsar connects to the Nebula network. They will be erased when the network disconnects.
strings.switchUseHostsLabel: Enable host name resolution when connected to Nebula network
strings.modalDeleteStaticHostConfirm: Are you sure you want to delete this static host?
strings.modalDeleteHostConfirm: Are you sure you want to delete this host?
strings.modalConnectionPortBlurb: Set to 0 to allow any port to connect.
strings.modalConnectionHostGroupBlurb: Either Host or Group must be filled in. If both are provided, the value in Host will be used.
strings.modalDeleteConnectionConfirm: Are you sure you want to delete this connection?
strings.modalEditConfigFileBlurb: You can edit the Nebula node .yaml configuration file directly below. If you don’t know what you are doing, there is a high likelihood of severely screwing up your connection. So make sure you back up the unedited file and then proceed with caution!
